Both realities report SQLite 3.53.4 and identical sqlite_source_id 2026-07-24 19:02:57 bf7c7f30031888f4e796e429ab3978879485813aaca6f641c7b33e4e09459bcc.

grf.hypothesis: Release-safe SQLite admission requires an independently authorized build-specific trust anchor; version and upstream source-id are necessary but not sufficient to identify the authorized productive runtime.
grf.strongest_counterhypothesis: SQLite version plus sqlite_source_id is sufficient because identical upstream source implies equivalent release-safety identity.
grf.falsifier: Construct two compile-time-divergent binaries from identical upstream 3.53.4 source, then compare admission under progressively stronger anchor field sets.

unusual_experiment.input: Downloaded immutable artifact from accepted-target workflow run 31523441341; no Frank database was opened or mutated.
unusual_experiment.interpretation: A build-specific fingerprint discriminates the observed counterworlds, but this experiment does not establish who controls the trusted fingerprint. A caller-supplied digest is consistency evidence, not independent authorization.

architecture_delta.statement: Bind Frank's accepted productive SQLite runtime to an independent build/artifact trust anchor that the caller cannot choose. Runtime admission must prove the loaded library matches that anchor before any canonical WAL DB open. Version and sqlite_source_id remain corroborating fields, not the authorization root.
architecture_delta.cross_gate_dependency: F-V01-13 cannot be cleanly closed by a caller-selected runtime manifest alone. The trust anchor should derive from the same owner-pinned trusted builder/artifact identity chain needed by F-V01-01, or from an equivalently independent deployment authority boundary.
architecture_delta.strongest_counterhypothesis: A separately anchored compile-options policy is enough without exact library/artifact identity.
architecture_delta.next_discriminating_test: On the accepted target, provision one owner/deployment-authorized fixed SQLite artifact and one equally self-consistent unauthorized sibling build; prove boot admits only the authorized artifact, rejects sibling/downgrade/library-swap before canonical state open, and preserves crash/restart continuity.
architecture_delta.rollback: Keep current V4 mechanisms as research candidates; do not promote product wiring until independent anchor authority and accepted-target boot integration are demonstrated.

negative_results.result: SQLite version plus sqlite_source_id cannot distinguish compile-time-divergent binaries built from the same upstream source.
A manifest digest supplied by the same caller selecting the manifest proves self-consistency but not independent authorization.

release_adjudication.reason: SQLite 3.53.4 itself is on the fixed side of the upstream WAL-reset boundary, but exact authorized productive runtime identity remains unproven.
release_adjudication.next_smallest_falsifier: Owner/deployment-pinned artifact trust anchor + accepted-target authorized-vs-sibling boot rejection matrix before any canonical WAL state open.
